transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Well, it's mostly work stuff. I'm an electrician, and what brings me in is I just keep going back over my jobs again and again. Like, I'll be checking the breakers, making sure the labels are right, checking the torque marks... speaking of labels, the shop actually just bought us these new Bluetooth label makers. They're supposed to be super high-tech and connect right to your phone, but honestly, they're a huge pain because my phone battery is always dead. My son—he's 14 now—he keeps borrowing my phone to watch these fishing videos on YouTube. Kid is completely obsessed with bass fishing all of a sudden, bought all this expensive gear for it... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Right, the jobs. So I'm taking photos of the panels, and sometimes I even drive all the way back to a site after I've already left. Just to check. I actually did that on Tuesday and the traffic on the interstate was backed up for miles because of some fender bender with a semi-truck. Took me an hour just to go three exits. But yeah, because of all this, a simple install is just taking me way longer than it should, and... well, the guys on the crew are starting to notice.
When you're not able to go back and check the jobs or feel like something might have been missed, does that cause you a lot of anxiety or distress?

Oh man, yeah, it really does. It just eats at me. Like, even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, and I closed it all up, this thought just keeps barging in on me. I start thinking, what if I missed one loose neutral? What if I left something in there that sparks and starts a fire? 

Which, actually, speaking of fires, my neighbor’s shed caught fire last summer. Complete total loss. He had this vintage riding mower in there—a John Deere from the 80s, I think? Beautiful machine. He spent like three years restoring the engine, finding original parts on eBay, and he was just devastated. The fire department said it was probably oily rags combusting or something, not electrical, but man, what a mess. The siding on his actual house even melted a little bit from the heat. 

But anyway, where was I? Right, the jobs. Yeah, I try to shake the thought off, you know? I tell myself the work is good and it's fine, but it just follows me all the way home. I'll be sitting in my truck or at the dinner table, and I can't even relax because I'm just picturing that panel.
Have you noticed these intrusive thoughts happening in other areas of your life, or do they only come up related to your work as an electrician?

Um, well, it's mostly just the work stuff. I mean, I don't really notice it happening with other things. Like, I'm not checking the stove or the locks at home a hundred times, if that's what you mean. Though, actually, my wife just had this whole new smart lock system installed on the front door. It's one of those ones with the keypad and the fingerprint scanner? She got it on sale at Home Depot. The guy there told her it was top of the line, but honestly, it's been glitching. Yesterday, it wouldn't even read my fingerprint because I had a little grease on my thumb from working on the truck. I had to use the actual key, which kind of defeats the whole purpose of a smart lock, you know? 

And the truck, man, that's a whole other thing. The transmission has been slipping, and I took it to this mechanic down on 4th Street. He tried to tell me I needed a whole rebuild, quoted me like three grand. I told him he was out of his mind. I mean, I know my way around an engine well enough to know it's probably just the solenoid. 

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the thoughts. Yeah, no, it's pretty much just the electrical jobs. I don't really get that feeling with anything else.

When these thoughts come up about possibly missing something on the job, do you feel driven to do something — like checking again, taking pictures, or going over your work in your mind — to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, that's really what brings me in, to be honest. I just keep going back over my jobs again and again. Like I was saying, I'll be checking the breakers, making sure all the labels are right, looking at the torque marks... 

Actually, speaking of torque, my buddy Dave just bought this crazy expensive digital torque wrench. Snap-on, I think? Cost him an arm and a leg. He’s always buying the newest tools, but half the time he doesn't even know how to calibrate them right. We were working this commercial gig last month, a big warehouse build-out, and he swore his wrench was set perfect, but I could tell just by feel it was way off. You know, when you've been doing this for twenty years, you just get a feel for it in your wrist. It's like muscle memory. 

But, uh, what was I saying? Right, the checking. Yeah, so I'll check all that stuff, and I take photos of the panels on my phone. Sometimes I'll even drive all the way back to a site after I've already left, just to look at it one more time and make sure it's safe. It's gotten to the point where a simple install is taking me way, way longer than it should. And like I said, the other guys on the crew are definitely starting to notice.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks or take these pictures in a certain way or a specific number of times to feel reassured or to prevent something bad from happening?

Um, no, not a specific number or anything like that. I don't have a rule where I have to look at it exactly three times or whatever. I just do it until I feel sure. Mostly I just scroll through the pictures on my phone. 

Which, man, my phone storage is completely maxed out right now because of all this. It's this older Samsung, and it keeps popping up with that annoying 'storage almost full' warning every single time I try to snap a photo. My daughter keeps telling me I need to back everything up to the cloud, but I don't really trust the cloud. I mean, where even is it, right? Some massive server farm out in the desert? I saw this special on TV a while back about how much power those data centers draw, and it’s just unbelievable. They have to build entire dedicated substations just to keep the cooling systems running so the servers don't melt down. Can you imagine the gauge of the feeder cables you'd need for a facility like that? Pulling that kind of wire would be an absolute nightmare, you'd need a whole crew just to manage the winch... 

But, uh, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, doing it a certain way. Yeah, no, there's no special routine to it. I just check and recheck until that nagging feeling finally backs off a little.
